name: Bazaar Balancer-fork exitPool without sender validation
summary: The Bazaar vault is a Balancer fork whose exitPool() never checks that the caller is the position holder or an approved relayer of it. The attacker called exitPool naming another holder as the sender, burning 850,000,000 of that holder’s BZR pool tokens and receiving the corresponding 392.37 WETH and 880,539,680 rYOLO.
notes: Non-upgradeable contract. The runtime code hash is 0xc0538736e15021b4d9f6eb211b35a54de0595fc7a28fcdf96cff7d6671337fa9 both at the deployment block 4573443 and at block 4619716, and the EIP-1967 implementation slot is zero, so no code change occurred between deployment and the exploit.

The whole loss is in the single exploit transaction, which is a contract creation whose constructor performs the exit. The vault 0xefb4e3cc438ef2854727a7df0d0baf844484edab pays out exactly 392.368916281212373207 WETH and 880539680.680963671973966099 rYOLO to the attacker contract while 850,000,000 BZR pool tokens are burned from the holder 0xb66585c4e460d49154d50325ce60adc44bc900e9. DefiLlama has no price series for rYOLO, so that component is recorded in quantity only and the USD total counts the WETH leg alone, which makes the figure a floor. WETH on Blast is priced through the DefiLlama ETH series. The attacker, self-described as a whitehat, forwarded the ETH to 0xfb72b2b32740de44488db791d83125ce39a53d91, which returned 353.13201 ETH to 0xde4d48f64687888d112b653c8fab4f0f67c37dbb in 0x5fc22cab25e0d9cf436718a040893550c266789ebd58c7ab5936634c762a70dd (block 4623649); the rYOLO never left the attacker contract. Recoveries do not reduce gross loss.
